data.narrative:
Anthrogen is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Ankit Singhal, Connor Lee, and Vignesh Karthik, having raised $4M to date. The company operates within a broader Biotech & Health sector universe comprising 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. Stage-Progression, using the $4M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression from Seed to next stage, yields an implied valuation of $10M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow biotech cohort; only 7 same-sector peers exist, but none met the minimum threshold of three datapoints within relevant valuation tiers. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be deployed because Anthrogen's revenue figures are not on file, preventing application of the sector's 6.6x median P/S multiple observed across the three public comps.

The triangulated valuation range of $8M–$12M (median $10M) reflects the single applicable methodology and carries material uncertainty. The low-to-high spread of $4M accounts for variance in stage-up assumptions and timing. Key limitations include the absence of revenue disclosure, sparse seed-stage private peer data, and reliance on a single method. This range should be validated through operational milestones, capital efficiency metrics, and narrower peer identification as additional data becomes available.
